topic: Managing 40 client work permits in a shared Excel — what the first missed expiry actually costs
format: State the uncomfortable truth about how most Oman businesses handle this problem — be specific and honest, not preachy
post:
One permit expired on a Tuesday.

Nobody caught it until the Ministry of Labour audit three weeks later.

The company had 40 employees on work permits. All tracked in a shared Excel file. Colour-coded tabs. A "responsible" person who hadn't opened the sheet in two weeks because she was handling a payroll dispute.

The fine wasn't the worst part.

The worst part was that the employee had been working illegally for 23 days — and the client relationship that took 18 months to build was now at risk because the business owner had to explain it.

This is how work permit tracking Oman businesses rely on actually fails. Not with a dramatic system crash. With a tab nobody refreshed.

When you're managing 10 permits, a spreadsheet is fine. At 40, it's a liability. Someone has to remember to check it. Someone has to own the renewal. Someone has to be available when they're not.
